overview:
Chrissy Houlahan seeks a new term in this southeastern Pennsylvania district, which leans Democratic by about six points. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, holding roughly $4 million on hand after raising $1.8 million, while Republican Marty Young has raised about $411 thousand and has $213 thousand available. No outside groups have spent against her.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, money, and the broader political environment, all of which favor the incumbent. Prediction markets also price Houlahan as a heavy favorite. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any specific sign of a competitive contest.
